Subject: Dedicated capacity provisioning — spare-pool governance & hot-standby policy

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a concise proposal that maps the committed Dedicated slab in the deal to a small hot-standby ("spare pool") we recommend holding for short-term bursts and failover. The key ideas:

- Primary reserved slab sized for steady-state production QPS (pinned).
- Hot-standby pool (5-12% of committed GPUs depending on workload burstiness) for sub-10s latency spikes, billed as reserved-but-dormant until used.
- Autoscale ladder: guaranteed headroom, burst credits that draw from the hot-standby first, then opportunistic GPU pool.
- Eviction & preemption rules that protect your SLA during high contention.

I attached a capacity matrix with two scenarios (conservative and aggressive) plus a draft SLA addendum for the hot-standby behavior. Can you confirm whether Solace prefers the 5% or the 10% standby option? Also looping in Karthik for commercial alignment.

Next steps:
1) You confirm target standby percentage and expected peak concurrency window (15m/60m).
2) We finalize the SLA addendum and hand to procurement/legal.
3) Ops (Jasmine) will provide a short runbook for eviction and fallback lines.

Best,

Sophie — good questions. Short answers up front, then specifics below:

1) Pricing: standby is a two-component model in our proposal — a small baseline standby reservation (flat monthly fee per GPU) + a usage overlay when the hot-standby is activated (per-token compute usage). For rough math, 10% standby increases committed cost ~6.2% in our conservative worksheet; see capacity_matrix_solace_q3.csv.

2) Failover order: traffic routes to the hot-standby pinned pool with identical model weights and quantization profile (no quality regression), then to opportunistic pool if hot-standby exhausted — opportunistic is best-effort and may use lower-precision variants.

3) Eviction: our standard is a ramped eviction signal: 5-minute soft notice (graceful scale-down hooks), then a 60-second hard preempt if needed. I flagged Jasmine to propose a shortened 2-minute escalation window for Solace since you asked.

More detail below:
- Billing example (from capacity_matrix): committed 200 GPUs, 10% standby = 20 GPUs; standby reservation = 20 * $X/month; expected monthly overlay if used <= 8% of committed compute spend under our burst profile.
- Quality fallback: hot-standby mirrors primary (same model version); opportunistic uses quantized variant with up to ~7% perf delta (model dependent).
- Ops hooks: prewarm on predicted load signals (webhook from your telemetry), immediate prefix caching transfer to standby after 30s sustained spike.

Karthik — can you confirm whether 10% standby is ok commercially? Jasmine — could you draft the 2-minute eviction play and the prewarm webhook contract we can include in SLA addendum?

Thanks,
Ben

Hi all — ops confirmation and proposed runbook (high level):

1) Hot-standby sizing: we recommend 8-10% for Solace given the 95th->99th percentile burst profile you showed us. 10% will cover typical 30-120s spikes without recovery optimization.

2) Prewarm & cache handoff: when telemetry signals predicted burst (user-defined webhook), we prewarm KV caches to the standby nodes and copy prefix state (30s lag). We'll include a webhook spec in the doc.

3) Eviction & notices: we can implement the 2-minute soft notice (HTTP callback with 120s TTL) and a final 60s forced-preempt. We will also emit trace events to your S3/Logging endpoint for 100% observability during eviction events.

4) Failover QA: we will run a two-week pre-production soak that simulates burst profiles at 1.2x expected concurrency; results will be delivered as a short ops report.

Attachments: I prepared a short "eviction-playbook.md" and the finalized capacity matrix (attached). See attachments included in Ben's original email; I've added the eviction-playbook to our internal draft.

If Solace confirms 10% standby and accepts the 90k GPU-minute credit ask (Karthik), ops can bake the final hooks in the SLA addendum and schedule the pre-prod soak next week.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
